newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold, Stop & Shop owner, reports profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Ahold, Stop & Shop owner, reports profit rise.

text.p: Dutch supermarkets group Ahold NV, owner of the Stop & Shop group, said Thursday its second-quarter net profits rose 18.3 percent to 121.3 million guilders ($73.1 million) from 102.5 million ($61.7 million).
Ahold, which generates half of its sales in the United States, said second-quarter revenues rose to 7.83 billion guilders ($4.7 billion) from 6.76 billion ($4.1 billion).
The group reiterated its earlier forecast that earnings for the whole of 1996 would be higher than in 1995.
Ahold said the recently acquired U.S. Stop & Shop chain would contribute to the rise in profits.
"Further growth of profits per share is expected to be positively affected by this takeover," it said.
Second-quarter earnings were at the high end of analysts' forecasts, which ranged from 111 million to 123 million guilders ($66.9 million to $74.1 million).
